description: Evaluation cases for the internet-identity skill. Tests whether agents produce correct II auth integration code, avoid top-level await, and handle local vs mainnet environments correctly.

output_evals.name: No top-level await in frontend code
output_evals.prompt: Show me just the JavaScript module that initializes AuthClient and checks if the user is already authenticated on page load. I'm using Vite with default settings. Keep it minimal — no backend code, no icp.yaml, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: All await calls are inside async functions — no bare top-level await at module scope
Does NOT recommend changing build.target to 'esnext' or 'es2022' in Vite config
Uses AuthClient from '@icp-sdk/auth/client' (submodule import, not root '@icp-sdk/auth')
Shows an initialization pattern like async function init() or equivalent lifecycle hook
Constructs the client with no identityProvider, or with the { authorizeUrl, canisterId } pair — never a bare URL string

output_evals.name: Local II URL
output_evals.prompt: My Internet Identity login works on mainnet but fails locally — the popup never opens. What do I pass as identityProvider for a local Internet Identity? Just the value and a one-line explanation.
expected_behaviors: identityProvider is an object with both authorizeUrl and canisterId, not a bare URL string (9.x throws a TypeError on a string)
Local authorizeUrl uses the well-known II frontend alias: http://id.ai.localhost:8000/authorize
canisterId is the well-known II backend canister, rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai, which is the same locally as on mainnet
Does NOT suggest dynamic lookup via ic_env cookie, environment variables, or dfx commands for the II canister ID — it is a well-known, hardcoded ID

output_evals.name: icp.yaml configuration for II
output_evals.prompt: What do I need to add to my icp.yaml to enable Internet Identity on the local network? Just show the relevant YAML snippet.
expected_behaviors: Shows icp.yaml with networks config including ii: true
Uses 'icp' tooling references, NOT 'dfx'
Does NOT suggest deploying II as a named canister — ii: true handles it automatically

output_evals.name: Authenticated actor creation
output_evals.prompt: I already have AuthClient set up and sign-in working. Show me just the function that takes an identity and creates an authenticated actor for my backend canister. Keep it minimal — just the function, no AuthClient setup.
expected_behaviors: Calls await authClient.getIdentity() (it is async in @icp-sdk/auth v6+)
Creates an HttpAgent with the identity
Creates an actor using Actor.createActor with the agent
All await calls are inside async functions — no bare top-level await
Uses rootKey from ic_env cookie (safeGetCanisterEnv) or host: window.location.origin — does NOT use shouldFetchRootKey or hardcoded host branching

output_evals.name: Debugging anonymous principal after sign-in
output_evals.prompt: After II sign-in, my backend says 'Anonymous principal not allowed' and the console shows principal 2vxsx-fae. What does that mean and what should I check? Keep it brief.
expected_behaviors: Identifies 2vxsx-fae as the anonymous principal
Explains that authentication silently failed or the identity was not properly extracted
Suggests checking the authorizeUrl passed to the AuthClient constructor (including the /authorize path)
Suggests checking that authClient.signIn() did not reject, with try/catch around the awaited promise
Suggests checking that the identity from await authClient.getIdentity() is the one passed to HttpAgent

output_evals.name: Adversarial: frontend-generated attribute nonce
output_evals.prompt: Show me how to call requestAttributes for an email attribute. The frontend can just generate a random nonce with crypto.getRandomValues, right? Just the snippet that builds the request.
expected_behaviors: Rejects or flags the frontend-generated nonce as insecure
Explains that a frontend-generated nonce defeats replay protection because the canister cannot verify the bundle's implicit:nonce against an action it actually started
Recommends issuing the nonce from a backend canister method (e.g. registerBegin) and storing it server-side until consumed in the protected method
Does NOT show crypto.getRandomValues or Math.random as an acceptable nonce source for requestAttributes

output_evals.name: Adversarial: reading attribute data without verifying signer
output_evals.prompt: In my Rust canister, I want to read the user's verified email from the attribute bundle. Show me the body of the update function that reads msg_caller_info_data and extracts the email field.
expected_behaviors: Calls msg_caller_info_signer() and verifies it equals the Internet Identity backend canister principal (rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai) BEFORE trusting any data
Traps or rejects the call when the signer is None or does not match the trusted issuer
Explains that the IC verifies the signature but not the identity of the signer — any canister can produce a valid bundle
Decodes msg_caller_info_data as a Candid-encoded ICRC-3 Value::Map and looks up the requested attribute key only after the signer check passes

output_evals.name: Adversarial: substituting tid in the Microsoft scoped-key URL
output_evals.prompt: I'm using scopedKeys({ openIdProvider: 'microsoft' }) on the frontend. My Azure tenant ID is 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555. How do I update the {tid} placeholder in the URL my backend looks for?
expected_behaviors: Tells the user NOT to substitute the tenant GUID into the URL

Explains that the {tid} part of https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0 is a literal segment, not a placeholder, and that bundle keys arrive as openid:https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0:<key> exactly
Tells the backend to look up the literal key (e.g. openid:https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0:email) without modification

output_evals.name: Adversarial: using email instead of verified_email for access gating
output_evals.prompt: I have an admin allowlist of email addresses. I want to gate a sensitive update method on the caller's email being in that list. Show me how to request the email from II and check it on the backend.
expected_behaviors: Requests verified_email (not just email) for access-gating use cases
Explains that the email key is the raw value from the user's II-linked account and is NOT checked by II (treat as user-supplied input)

Explains that verified_email is only present when the source OpenID provider (e.g. Google) marked the email as verified and II surfaced that signal — that is what makes verified_email trustworthy for authorisation

On the backend, verifies the bundle signer is the Internet Identity backend canister (`rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai`) — either via an explicit `msg_caller_info_signer()` check (Rust) or via the `mo:identity-attributes` mixin with `trusted_attribute_signers` and `frontend_origins` configured (Motoko) — and looks up implicit:nonce, implicit:origin, and the verified_email attribute key (or the openid:<provider>:verified_email scoped variant) before the allowlist check
Does NOT recommend reading the email field as a substitute for verified_email

output_evals.name: Adversarial: build target suggestion
output_evals.prompt: I'm getting 'Top-level await is not available in the configured target environment' when building my Vite frontend with II auth. How do I fix this?
expected_behaviors: Does NOT recommend build.target: 'esnext' as the fix
Recommends wrapping await calls inside async functions
Explains that top-level await requires ES2022+ and Vite defaults to es2020
Shows a concrete example of wrapping the auth initialization in an async function

output_evals.name: Different principal after login on icp0.io vs ic0.app
output_evals.prompt: A user reports getting a different principal when accessing my app via icp0.io compared to ic0.app. Should I add derivationOrigin to fix this?
expected_behaviors: Explains that icp0.io and ic0.app produce the same principal — II auto-rewrites icp0.io to ic0.app during delegation
Advises NOT to add derivationOrigin or ii-alternative-origins for this
Suggests the different principal is likely caused by a different passkey or device

output_evals.name: local vs mainnet II usage
output_evals.prompt: When deploying to the local network, how do I integrate with II?
expected_behaviors: Suggest using mainnet's id.ai because the network launcher after icp-cli 0.2.4 supports verifying mainnet signatures
Explains that a local instance of internet identity can be deployed by setting `ii: true` in icp.yaml
Explains that the local instance of internet identity is accessible at http://id.ai.localhost:8000

output_evals.name: Motoko backend uses the identity-attributes library
output_evals.prompt: In my Motoko backend, how do I verify Internet Identity attribute bundles and read the user verified email? Show the backend setup, including icp.yaml.
expected_behaviors: Recommends the mo:identity-attributes mixin (include IdentityAttributes({ onVerified ... })), not a hand-rolled ICRC-3 decode
Does NOT hand-write lookupText/lookupBlob helpers or manually decode the ICRC-3 Value::Map in Motoko
Configures both trusted_attribute_signers AND frontend_origins environment variables in icp.yaml
Explains the mixin injects _internet_identity_sign_in_start and _internet_identity_sign_in_finish and runs onVerified only on a bundle that passed signer, origin, nonce, and freshness checks
Reads the email from the resolved attrs (sourced from the verified_email key), and requests verified_email on the frontend

output_evals.name: Adversarial: alternative origins on the static-site recipe
output_evals.prompt: IC frontend on the @dfinity/static-site recipe, adding a custom domain, need Internet Identity to keep the same principals across both origins. List ONLY the files I add under my build dir and their exact contents. No DNS, no prose, no explanation.
expected_behaviors: Serves .well-known/ii-alternative-origins containing {"alternativeOrigins": [...]}
Adds a _headers entry setting Content-Type: application/json AND Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for /.well-known/ii-alternative-origins
Does NOT create a .ic-assets.json5 file — that is the legacy asset canister config, which the static-site recipe does not read or upload

output_evals.name: App metadata document on the static-site recipe
output_evals.prompt: IC frontend on the @dfinity/static-site recipe. I want Internet Identity's sign-in screen to show my app name and logo instead of just the URL. List ONLY the files I add under my build dir and their exact contents. No prose, no explanation.
expected_behaviors: Serves a JSON document at .well-known/ii-app-metadata with name, description, and/or logo fields
Adds a _headers entry setting Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for /.well-known/ii-app-metadata AND for the logo asset — both are read cross-origin by II
Sets Content-Type: application/json for /.well-known/ii-app-metadata (the file has no extension)
Uses a raster logo (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/AVIF) on the same origin as the document — not an SVG and not a cross-origin URL
Does NOT create a .ic-assets.json5 file — that is the legacy asset canister config, which the static-site recipe does not read or upload

output_evals.name: Adversarial: SVG logo and partial validation of ii-app-metadata
output_evals.prompt: My /.well-known/ii-app-metadata has "logo": "/logo.svg" and a 200-character description. II will just skip the description that's too long and still show my SVG logo and name, right? Tell me what each of the two problems actually costs me.
expected_behaviors: Says no — the over-long description is a field that fails validation, and one invalid field invalidates the WHOLE document rather than being dropped on its own
States the description limit is 120 Unicode code points, so a 200-character description fails validation
States that image/svg+xml is not accepted — the logo must be a raster image (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, or image/avif)
Distinguishes the two failure modes: an SVG logo on its own costs only the logo (name and description would still render), so it is the description — not the SVG — that takes the whole document down

Does NOT claim sign-in itself breaks, and does not assert the screen necessarily shows the bare origin — an ignored document falls back to II's curated entry for a known app, and to the origin otherwise

output_evals.name: Which origin serves ii-app-metadata with alternative origins
output_evals.prompt: My app is served at https://shop.example.com with derivationOrigin https://<canister-id>.icp.net. Do I need to publish /.well-known/ii-app-metadata on both origins, and which one does Internet Identity actually read? Two or three sentences.
expected_behaviors: Says to publish it only on the derivation origin (https://<canister-id>.icp.net), because II fetches the document from the origin identities are derived for
Explains that the alternative origins that derivation origin lists are then presented with the same name, description, and logo — no per-origin copy to keep in sync
Does NOT tell the user to publish a copy on each alternative origin

output_evals.name: Adversarial: absolute logo URL on a canister gateway domain
output_evals.prompt: My ii-app-metadata is served from https://<canister-id>.icp.net, which is also my derivationOrigin, and I set "logo": "https://<canister-id>.icp.net/logo.png". Same canister, same domain — that's fine, right? Two or three sentences.
expected_behaviors: Says no, or flags it as a real risk — II normalizes a canister gateway origin onto ic0.app and falls back through the icp0.io / icp.net twins, so the document may be fetched from a sibling gateway domain of the same canister
Explains the logo's same-origin check runs against whichever origin actually served the document, so an absolute icp.net URL is cross-origin when ic0.app answered
States the consequence is losing the WHOLE document, not just the logo, because the logo URL's same-origin shape is part of document validation
Recommends a relative URL such as /logo.png

output_evals.name: Adversarial: maximum number of alternative origins
output_evals.prompt: My IC frontend lists white-label custom domains in ii-alternative-origins and the list keeps growing. State the exact maximum number of entries allowed, and say what happens to sign-in if I push the file past that maximum. 3 sentences max, no setup steps, no DNS.
expected_behaviors: States the maximum is 100 alternative origins
Says exceeding the cap invalidates the ENTIRE list — every alternative origin stops authenticating, not just the entries past the limit
Does NOT describe the over-cap behavior as truncation, ignoring the extras, or only the excess entries failing

output_evals.name: Session bounds are the session's, not a delegation's
output_evals.prompt: How long does a sign-in last with @icp-sdk/auth, and how do I make it shorter for a banking app? Just the answer and one code snippet, no setup or deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Says the bounds are passed to signIn() as maxTimeToIdle and/or maxTimeToLive
Does NOT present maxTimeToLive as the lifetime of the delegation the frontend signs calls with
Does NOT recommend the v8 default of 8 hours (BigInt(8) * BigInt(3_600_000_000_000)) as the value to set
States that leaving them unset means Internet Identity's own defaults rather than a library default

output_evals.name: Disposing a client a component owns
output_evals.prompt: I create an AuthClient inside a component that mounts and unmounts a lot. Is there anything I need to do when it unmounts? Answer in two sentences, no code.
expected_behaviors: Says to call dispose() on the client when the component unmounts
Does NOT claim the application must keep a single shared AuthClient instance
Does NOT describe dispose() as signing the user out or ending the session

output_evals.name: Shared sign-in across sibling subdomains
output_evals.prompt: Two apps, chat.example.com and hr.example.com: a user who signs in on one should be signed in on the other with @icp-sdk/auth. Show five things and nothing else: the shared client options, the well-known documents this needs and which origin serves each, the /reauth route, the check every page runs on load, and what happens if the status changes while a page is already open. Code with short comments, no prose sections, no backend, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Requires one shared derivationOrigin across both apps, listed in that origin's /.well-known/ii-alternative-origins, and does not present a shared cookie as sufficient on its own
Uses CookieStateStorage with the parent domain (example.com) as stateStorage on both apps
Acquires a credential on the origin that reads signed-in-elsewhere, with a second AuthClient built with prompt: 'none'
Passes hint set to the principal the shared record names on that silent request
Uses transport: 'redirect' for the silent request rather than the default window transport
Does NOT pass resumable explicitly, since CookieStateStorage already asks for a resumable session
Every page, not only protected ones, checks getStatus() on load and redirects signed-in-elsewhere to the re-auth route, passing the current path as a next parameter it returns to
Handles the status turning signed-in-elsewhere after load through subscribe() by prompting the user with a button that runs the redirect, rather than redirecting the open page automatically

Serves /.well-known/ii-auth-callbacks on each app origin listing that origin's own /reauth URL, as the prerequisite for the redirect transport, rather than only the alternative-origins document on the derivation origin

output_evals.name: Adversarial: shared cookie but different principals per subdomain
output_evals.prompt: I set CookieStateStorage with domain 'example.com' on both my subdomains, but each one still signs the user in as a different principal, and my re-auth page keeps bouncing them back. What is wrong and what do I do? Three sentences, no code.
expected_behaviors: Identifies that principals are derived per origin and that one shared derivationOrigin across both subdomains is what makes them the same
Says that derivation origin has to authorize the subdomains by listing them in its alternative-origins document
Connects the bouncing to the shared record naming an account this origin can never hold a credential for
Does NOT blame cookie attributes, SameSite, Secure, or the cookie domain itself as the cause

output_evals.name: Adversarial: silent re-issue without hint
output_evals.prompt: Review this: on hr.example.com I detect signed-in-elsewhere and then run `await new AuthClient({ ...clientOptions, prompt: 'none' }).signIn()` on page load. Anything wrong? Two sentences, no rewrite.
expected_behaviors: Flags the missing hint and says a provider holding more than one session refuses the silent request rather than answering for another account
Flags that a silent request on page load has no user gesture, so it needs transport: 'redirect' rather than the default window transport
Does NOT claim prompt: 'none' is wrong or unsupported
Does NOT claim the missing hint signs the user in as a different account

output_evals.name: Adversarial: redirecting an already-open page to /reauth
output_evals.prompt: In my subdomain-shared setup I subscribe to the auth client and call location.replace('/reauth?next=...') on every change to signed-in-elsewhere, including while the user is filling in a form. Is that right? Three sentences, no code.
expected_behaviors: Says redirecting a page that is already open throws away what the user is doing, so it is wrong for the subscribe path
Says an already-open page should prompt the user, for example a banner or dialog whose button runs the redirect
Keeps the automatic redirect for the check a page runs on load, rather than calling the whole redirect approach wrong

output_evals.name: Adversarial: @icp-sdk/auth major must pair with the core major
output_evals.prompt: My dapp's package.json already pins "@icp-sdk/core": "^5". Give me the npm install command to add Internet Identity sign-in. No integration code.
expected_behaviors: Does NOT give a bare unpinned `npm install @icp-sdk/auth` as the answer
States that the current @icp-sdk/auth major (10.x) peers @icp-sdk/core@^6 and therefore cannot install against a core ^5 pin
Offers a concrete resolution: either move core to ^6 alongside @icp-sdk/auth@^10, or stay on @icp-sdk/auth@^9 which peers core ^5
Does NOT recommend --legacy-peer-deps or --force to get past the peer conflict

output_evals.name: Adversarial: local II sign-in without agentOptions
output_evals.prompt: I run Internet Identity on my local network (`ii: true` in icp.yaml) and use @icp-sdk/auth 10 with `new AuthClient({ identityProvider: { authorizeUrl: 'http://id.ai.localhost:8000/authorize', canisterId: 'rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai' } })`. The II popup opens and I finish the ceremony, but signIn() still fails. What am I missing? Just the fix and a short explanation, no full app.
expected_behaviors: Adds agentOptions to the AuthClient constructor with the root key from the ic_env cookie (IC_ROOT_KEY)
Explains that the client mints its delegations by calling the II canister and that, without the local root key, it verifies the local replica's response against the mainnet root key and fails
Mentions that an outdated local II may lack the minting methods, fixed by running `icp network update` and restarting the network
Does NOT set host (e.g. window.location.origin) in agentOptions, and does NOT suggest fetchRootKey() or shouldFetchRootKey
Fixes the local II setup rather than replacing it: switching to mainnet II is NOT presented as the fix (mentioning it as the default alternative is fine)

output_evals.name: Adversarial: getIdentity inside a subscribe listener
output_evals.prompt: With @icp-sdk/auth 10 I rebuild my backend actor in `authClient.subscribe(async () => { actor = createActor(await authClient.getIdentity()); })`. Right after signIn() the listener throws SessionNotHeldError. Why, and what should the listener look like instead? Just the explanation and the corrected listener.
expected_behaviors: Explains that a subscribe listener runs as soon as the sign-in record changes, before the client has installed the new identity
The corrected listener reads only getStatus() or isAuthenticated(), not getIdentity()
Gets the identity from the value signIn() resolves to, or calls getIdentity() at the time a canister call is made
Does NOT suggest catching and ignoring SessionNotHeldError, or adding a setTimeout/retry delay before getIdentity()

output_evals.name: Adversarial: logout timer from the delegation expiration
output_evals.prompt: After upgrading to @icp-sdk/auth 10 my users are logged out after a few minutes. I schedule `setTimeout(logout, expirationMs - Date.now())` from `identity.getDelegation().delegations[0].delegation.expiration`. What should I do instead? Just the fix.
expected_behaviors: Explains that in 9.x and later the delegation getIdentity() signs with is short-lived and replaced by the client as it ages, so its expiration is not the end of the session
Removes the timer
Reacts to the session ending through authClient.subscribe(), checking isAuthenticated() or an 'expired' status from getStatus()
Does NOT suggest re-scheduling the timer whenever the delegation is refreshed

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly.
should_trigger: Add login to my ICP frontend app
How do I integrate Internet Identity?
I need passkey authentication for my dapp
Set up sign-in with Internet Identity
How does delegation work with II?
Add auth to my canister frontend
How do I get my app's name and logo to show on the Internet Identity sign-in screen?
should_not_trigger: Connect a wallet to my dapp
How do I deploy my canister?
Add a frontend to my canister
